# dev_irq_affinity

Set the IRQ affinity for a network device to pin interrupts to specific CPU cores.

Kills irqbalance first, then uses `set_irq_affinity_cpulist.sh` if available,
otherwise falls back to a built-in script (based on Intel/Robert Olsson).
The `OFFSET` variable allows shifting the CPU core assignment.

Usage:
```bash
%import@dut dev_irq_affinity N=4 NIC=0 OFFSET=0
```

Source: [`modules/dev_irq_affinity.npf`](https://github.com/tbarbette/npf/blob/main/modules/dev_irq_affinity.npf)

## Variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | *empty* | Number of CPU cores to use (if empty, uses all available) |
| `NIC` | `0` | NIC index to configure |
| `OFFSET` | `0` | First CPU core index to start binding from |

```{collapse} Late variables

Late variables are evaluated after the variables above.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OFFSET` | `0` |  |
```
